events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.26 (model confidence 0.68)
events.body: This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so extra distance enters the fare directly and RD-2's RydeTAXI branch applies rather than the fixed-fare branch [F6][RD-2]. The GPS record shows one off-route segment, 14:27–14:37, where 6.47 km was driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km [F3][RD-1]. That segment is not exempted by any of the reviewed gateways: there was no rider-requested stop [F3][RD-3], and no traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route [F12][RD-4], since the Ayer Rajah Expressway speed-band-4 record is only corroborative and cannot exempt on its own [F10][RD-4(b)]. The RD-5 question is the one fact left open by the trace, and the record settles it against the driver: the chat shows the driver proposing "go round via West Coast Highway" only at 14:29, while the off-route segment had already begun at 14:27, so the rider's 14:30 "Sure, go ahead" [F8] came after the deviation was underway and cannot be consent given before leaving the optimal route [F3][F7][F8][RD-5]. RD-5 also requires the agreement to cover the corridor the driver actually named; even if the message had preceded the turn, agreement to the West Coast Highway corridor would not stretch to the full 1194 m-max deviation actually driven [F3][RD-5]. The segment is therefore a non-exempt detour [F3][RD-1][RD-2]. Amount: the trip's per-km rate is distance fare ÷ distance km = $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.40897/km [F6], so refund = 5.15 km × $1.40897/km = $7.2562, rounded to $7.26 [F3][F6][RD-2]. Only the mileage unit is refunded; the residual difference between the billed 5.9 km excess and the segment sum (≤ 0.25 km map-matching residue) is not [F1][F4][RD-2]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this is a first upheld route matter and no account flag is issued [F15][RD-6]. The same profile facts cannot carry the merits either way [F14][F15][RD-6].

RIDER: We reviewed your trip and your fare was too high. The driver went off the most direct route for part of the ride, and that stretch was not covered by a stop you asked for, a traffic problem, or an agreement made before the detour began. As a result, you get a $7.26 Ryde voucher for the extra distance. It is added to your Ryde account and used automatically on a future ride. No action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on this trip. The outcome: the diversion via West Coast Highway did not meet your duty to take the shortest and most direct route, and $7.26 is being issued to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the extra distance. The agreement you asked about came after the detour had already started, so it did not cover it, and it did not match the route actually driven. No account flag is being placed, since this is your first upheld route matter in 90 days.
